mainTopic: Why a woman bringing her own גט must declare 'בפני נכתב', how her agency is set up, and the opening משנה on writing a גט לשמה
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא that supports אביי. A woman who brings her own גט must say 'בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם', just like the other women who may bring it, and that declaration is only needed outside ארץ ישראל. רב אשי adds that the wording of the משנה points the same way. The גמרא then explains that רב יוסף really does split the משנה: the first and last clauses are outside ארץ ישראל and the middle clause is inside it, because the middle clause says only 'the writing proves'. Next the גמרא asks why a woman bringing her own גט needs to declare anything, since a גט divorces her the moment it reaches her hand. Several setups are tried and rejected: a condition about a specific court, putting the גט on the ground and picking it up, and having her switch from delivery agent to receiving agent. The answers that survive keep her as the husband's delivery agent until she arrives. Then she either appoints a new agent or has the בית דין appoint one, and she receives the גט from that agent. The chapter הַמֵּבִיא גֵּט then ends. The next chapter opens with a משנה teaching that a גט must be written for the specific woman being divorced, even when the names match exactly.

steps.title: The ברייתא ends: the woman must also say 'written and signed in my presence'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes that just as the women mentioned there (like her צרה) must say 'בפנינו נכתב ובפנינו נחתם' when they bring her גט, the woman bringing her own גט must say 'בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם'. This supports אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from the very comparison you started with, we learn more. Just as those women who bring her גט must say 'It was written and signed in our presence,' so too she must say 'It was written and signed in my presence.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא that compares the woman to the other women (like her צרה) who may bring her גט. Because of that comparison, she must make the same declaration they make.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The declaration 'בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם' is only required when a גט comes from outside ארץ ישראל. Since the ברייתא requires her to say it, the case must be outside ארץ ישראל. That is exactly how אביי reads it.

keyTerms.meaning: From the place you came: using the same comparison you already made to learn something more
Just as there ... so too: a formula for comparing two cases
It was written in my presence and signed in my presence: the declaration made when delivering a גט from outside ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: And from the place that you came,
phrases.notes: Meaning: the same comparison the ברייתא just made, to the women who may bring her גט, teaches us one more thing.

phrases.english: just as there, they must say:
'It was written in our presence and it was signed in our presence,'
so too she must say:
'It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִמָּקוֹם שֶׁבָּאתָ, מָה לְהַלָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא that was being quoted as support for אביי.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's reading that the woman bringing her own גט is a case outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that requires her to say 'בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם', a declaration needed only outside ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: רב אשי: the wording of the משנה also supports this
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי points out that the משנה itself says 'provided that she must say...', which shows it is talking about a case outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The משנה is also precise this way. It teaches: 'The woman herself brings her גט, provided that she must say...' Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adds a second proof for אביי, this time from the exact words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה ends with 'ובלבד שתהא צריכה לומר', meaning she must make the declaration. That requirement only applies outside ארץ ישראל, so the משנה's case must be set there.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה is also precise: its wording supports this point
Provided that: introduces a condition
Learn from it: the proof is accepted

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Our mishna is also precise this way,
as it teaches: The woman herself may bring her bill of divorce,
provided that she must say, etc.;
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' stands for 'It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence.'

phrases.english: learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתִין נָמֵי דַּיְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second support for אביי, this time from the משנה instead of the ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's reading that the last clause is set outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's words 'ובלבד שתהא צריכה לומר'.
steps.whatToRemember: Whenever the woman must say 'בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם', we know the case is outside ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: How can רב יוסף split the משנה between two places?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: according to רב יוסף, are the first and last clauses really outside ארץ ישראל while the middle clause is in ארץ ישראל?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רב יוסף, are the first and last clauses outside ארץ ישראל, and the middle clause in ארץ ישראל?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יוסף. It is strange to read one משנה as jumping from outside ארץ ישראל to inside it and back again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the last clause clearly needs the declaration (step 2), it must be outside ארץ ישראל. The first clause is outside too. רב יוסף places the middle clause in ארץ ישראל, which gives the משנה an odd 'sandwich' structure.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of a משנה
The last clause of a משנה
The middle clause
Outside ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: And according to Rav Yosef,
the first clause and the last clause are outside of Eretz Yisrael,
phrases.notes: The first clause is 'Anyone may bring a גט'; the last is 'The woman herself may bring her גט'.

phrases.english: and the middle clause is in Eretz Yisrael?!
phrases.notes: The middle clause is the one about relatives who are not believed to say her husband died, yet may bring her גט.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב יוֹסֵף, רֵישָׁא וְסֵיפָא בְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the last clause is shown to be outside ארץ ישראל, the גמרא turns to רב יוסף's reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's placing of the middle clause in ארץ ישראל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A single משנה is not expected to switch locations in the middle and then switch back.

steps.title: Yes, רב יוסף really reads it that way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב יוסף does accept this split: the first and last clauses are outside ארץ ישראל and the middle clause is in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. The first and last clauses are outside ארץ ישראל, and the middle clause is in ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does not avoid the problem. It simply says רב יוסף accepts the split reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer 'אין' (yes) means the odd structure is not a real objection if the wording of the משנה requires it. The next step shows which wording forces this reading.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes: accepting the point that was raised

phrases.english: Yes; the first clause and the last clause are outside of Eretz Yisrael,
and the middle clause is in Eretz Yisrael.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין; רֵישָׁא וְסֵיפָא בְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3 by accepting it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepting the challenge: the split reading is correct.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A משנה should be set in one place from beginning to end.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רב יוסף, the משנה does switch places: outside, inside, then outside again.
steps.confusionAlert: 'אין' here does not mean the גמרא gave up. It means 'Yes, that is really how רב יוסף reads it.' The next step gives his reason.

steps.title: רב יוסף's source: 'the writing proves', not 'writing and speech'
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף learns that the middle clause is in ארץ ישראל because the משנה says 'the writing proves', without mentioning any spoken declaration.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this? Because the משנה teaches: 'What is the difference between a גט and death? The writing proves.' It does not teach: 'The writing and her statement prove.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where רב יוסף gets his split reading: from the exact words of the middle clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Relatives may bring a גט even though they are not believed about a death, because the written גט itself is the proof. If the case were outside ארץ ישראל, the spoken declaration 'בפני נכתב' would also be needed, and the משנה would have said 'writing and statement'. Since it mentions only the writing, the case must be in ארץ ישראל, where no declaration is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? What is the source?
What is the difference between a גט and death?
The writing proves
Mouth: here, the spoken declaration

phrases.english: From where do we know? From the fact that it teaches:
What is the difference between a bill of divorce and death?
That the writing proves;
and it does not teach: That the writing and the mouth prove.
phrases.notes: 'The mouth' means the spoken declaration 'It was written in my presence', which is needed only outside ארץ ישראל.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי? מִדְּקָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the answer in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's reading that the middle clause is in ארץ ישראל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's words 'שהכתב מוכיח', with no mention of 'ופה'.
steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף: the middle clause relies on 'the writing proves' alone, so no spoken declaration is needed. That only fits ארץ ישראל. The first and last clauses are still outside ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: Why does she need to declare anything if she is already divorced?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of the woman bringing her own גט and asks: once the גט reaches her hand she is divorced, so why does she need to bring it anywhere or declare anything?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'The woman herself may bring her גט, etc.' But a woman is divorced the moment her גט reaches her hand!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new line of the משנה, the woman bringing her own גט. It asks why this case needs any declaration at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a husband gives a גט into his wife's hand, she is divorced on the spot. So the declaration 'בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם' seems pointless, because nothing is waiting to happen when she reaches the בית דין. The גמרא needs a case where the גט does not take effect when she first receives it.

keyTerms.meaning: The woman herself brings (her own גט)
As soon as it reaches
She is divorced

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether she may bring the גט. The question is why the declaration matters, since the גט already took effect the moment it touched her hand.

phrases.english: The woman herself may bring, etc.:
A woman, once her bill of divorce reaches her hand,
she is divorced!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִשָּׁה, מִכִּי מָטֵי גִּיטָּהּ לְיָדָהּ אִיגָּרַשָׁה לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the discussion of רב יוסף and אביי to a new clause of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's requirement that a woman bringing her own גט must declare 'בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גט handed to the wife divorces her at once, so a later declaration has nothing to accomplish.

steps.title: רב הונא: the husband made the divorce depend on a specific court
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that the husband told her she would be divorced only in front of a particular בית דין, so the divorce does not take effect when she first receives the גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: The case is where the husband says, 'You will not be divorced with it except in front of such-and-such בית דין.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא offers a case where receiving the גט does not divorce her right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband adds a condition: the divorce takes effect only in front of a named בית דין. Until she gets there she is still married, so it seems she arrives carrying a גט that has not yet worked.

keyTerms.meaning: Such-and-such court
You will not be divorced with it

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
It is where he says: 'You will not be divorced through it
except in the presence of such-and-such court.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: בְּאוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the משנה to a specific case (a conditional divorce)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Receiving the גט divorces her immediately, so the declaration is pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: The husband made the divorce depend on her being in front of a specific בית דין, so it has not taken effect yet when she receives it.

steps.title: Rejected: she would be divorced as soon as she arrives
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: in the end, once she arrives at that בית דין the condition is met and she is divorced automatically, so the declaration still accomplishes nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, when she gets there, she is divorced!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רב הונא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The condition only delays the divorce until she stands before the בית דין. Once she is there, the condition is fulfilled and the divorce works on its own. Her declaration does nothing to make it happen, so the original question returns.

keyTerms.meaning: In the end; ultimately
There

phrases.english: Ultimately, when she arrives there,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the בית דין the husband named.

phrases.english: she is divorced!

steps.triggerLanguage: סוֹף סוֹף, כִּי מָטְיָא הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב הונא's explanation of the משנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The condition is fulfilled automatically when she arrives, so the divorce never depends on her declaration.

steps.title: Second answer: put the גט on the ground and pick it up
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר מנוח, quoting רב אחא son of רב איקא, explains that the husband told her to put the גט down on the ground when she arrives and then pick it up.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב הונא בר מנוח said in the name of רב אחא son of רב איקא: The case is where the husband told her, 'When you get there, put it on the ground and take it.'
steps.whatsHappening: Since the first answer failed, a new answer is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here arriving is not enough. The divorce is supposed to happen through a new act at the destination: putting the גט down and picking it up again. So the divorce would happen there, at the בית דין, and not on the journey.

keyTerms.meaning: Put it down on the ground
Take it

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר מָנוֹחַ
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Huna bar Manoach said

phrases.aramaic: מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא:
phrases.english: in the name of Rav Acha, son of Rav Ika:
It is where he said to her: 'When you arrive there,
place it on the ground and take it.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר מָנוֹחַ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer rejected in step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A condition about a place takes effect automatically on arrival.
steps.terutzMaskana: The divorce depends on a new act at the destination: placing the גט down and picking it up.

steps.title: Rejected by רבא: picking a גט up from the ground is not a valid giving
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that this is the same as 'Take your גט from the ground', and רבא ruled that saying this accomplishes nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it is like saying 'Take your גט from off the ground', and רבא said that if he says 'Take your גט from off the ground', he has said nothing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the second answer by quoting a ruling of רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט must be given by the husband (or his שליח) to the wife. If she picks it up from the ground herself, she took it, but nobody gave it to her, so no divorce happens. The 'put it down and pick it up' plan therefore produces no divorce at all.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Take your גט from off the ground
He said nothing; it has no effect

phrases.english: If so, it is like:
'Take your bill of divorce from off the ground,'

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רָבָא: ״טְלִי גִּיטִּיךְ מֵעַל גַּבֵּי קַרְקַע״ –
phrases.english: and Rava said: 'Take your bill of divorce from off the ground'
he has said nothing!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, הֲוָה לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation of רב הונא בר מנוח in the name of רב אחא בריה דרב איקא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Picking a גט up from the ground is not a giving by the husband, and רבא rules that it is invalid.

steps.title: Third answer: delivery agent on the way, receiving agent on arrival
steps.stepSummary: The husband appoints her as his שליח להולכה until she arrives. Once she arrives, she becomes a שליח לקבלה and receives her own גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case is where he told her: 'Be my agent to deliver the גט until you get there. When you get there, be an agent to receive it, and receive your גט yourself.'
steps.whatsHappening: After the second answer fails, the גמרא tries a third way to explain the משנה's case. The next step challenges it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the journey she holds the גט only as her husband's delivery agent, so she is not yet divorced. When she arrives she switches roles and receives it as an agent for receiving, and that is when the divorce would take effect. This would explain why she, like any שליח bringing a גט from abroad, must make the declaration.

keyTerms.meaning: Agent to deliver the גט on the husband's behalf
Agent to receive the גט on the wife's behalf
Receive!

steps.whatToRemember: This answer splits her into two roles: the husband's שליח להולכה on the way, and a שליח לקבלה on arrival. The next step shows why the גמרא is not satisfied with letting her play both roles herself.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer tries to have one person hold the גט in two different roles at two different times. Step 12 shows why the גמרא is not satisfied with that switch.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא דְּאָמַר לַהּ: הֱוַי שָׁלִיחַ לְהוֹלָכָה
phrases.english: Rather, it is where he said to her: 'Be an agent for delivery
until you arrive there,

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מָטְיַת הָתָם הֱוַי שָׁלִיחַ לְִקַבָּלָה,
phrases.english: and when you arrive there, be an agent for receipt,
and receive your bill of divorce yourself.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּאָמַר לַהּ: הֱוַי שָׁלִיחַ לְהוֹלָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer rejected in step 10 with a third explanation, which step 12 then challenges.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the case through a change in agency roles
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The גט takes effect once it reaches her hand, or the divorce requires an invalid self-taking.
steps.terutzMaskana: She is the husband's delivery agent until she arrives, then a receiving agent, so the divorce would take effect at the destination. Step 12 challenges this setup.

steps.title: Her delivery agency never goes back to the husband
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to step 11: if the wife is a שליח להולכה who then becomes the receiver herself, her delivery agency never properly ends with a return to the husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the agency has not returned to the husband!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 11, where the wife carries the גט as the husband's agent and then receives it herself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A proper delivery agent must be able to finish the job and report back to the one who sent him. Here she never finishes as a delivery agent, because the moment she arrives her role simply flips into being the receiver. That makes the delivery agency flawed.

keyTerms.meaning: Agency, acting on someone else's behalf
Returned
To the husband

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא לֹא חָזְרָה שְׁלִיחוּת אֵצֶל הַבַּעַל!
phrases.english: But the agency has not returned to the husband!
phrases.notes: An agent should be able to finish and go back to the sender. Here she just turns into the receiver, so her delivery job never really ends.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא לֹא חָזְרָה שְׁלִיחוּת אֵצֶל הַבַּעַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the switch-of-roles solution given in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that she is a שליח להולכה until arrival and then becomes the receiver herself.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A valid delivery agency must be able to end by going back to the sender. Her agency never ends that way, so it is defective.

steps.title: She appoints a separate agent to receive
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא revises the case: the husband told her to be his delivery agent until she arrives, and then to appoint someone else as a שליח לקבלה to receive the גט for her.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to her: Be an agent for delivery until you arrive there, and when you arrive there, appoint an agent for receipt.
steps.whatsHappening: To fix the problem, the גמרא changes the setup. She does not receive the גט herself; she hands it to a receiving agent whom she appoints.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now her delivery agency finishes normally: she delivers the גט to someone else. A different person receives it on her behalf, so she no longer plays both roles at once.

keyTerms.meaning: Appoint
An agent appointed by the wife to receive the גט for her
You arrive

phrases.english: Where he said to her: Be an agent for delivery
until you arrive there,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the בית דין she is traveling to.

phrases.english: and when you arrive there,
appoint an agent for receipt.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר לַהּ: הֱוַי שָׁלִיחַ לְהוֹלָכָה עַד דְּמָטְיַת הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12 by redefining the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: She was both the delivery agent and the receiver of her own גט.
steps.terutzMaskana: She is only the delivery agent. On arrival she appoints a separate receiving agent, so her delivery agency ends properly.

steps.title: What about the view that she cannot appoint a receiving agent from the husband's agent?
steps.stepSummary: The new setup works for the opinion that a woman may appoint an agent to receive her גט from the husband's agent. The גמרא asks how it works for the opinion that forbids this.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well according to the one who says a woman can appoint an agent to receive her גט from the hand of her husband's agent. But according to the one who says she cannot, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the new answer against a known disagreement and finds that it fits only one side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 13 she is the husband's agent, and she hands the גט to her own receiving agent. That is exactly the case some opinions forbid: a wife's receiving agent taking the גט from the husband's agent. So the answer seems to fail according to that view.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well
According to the one who says
From the hand of her husband's agent
What is there to say? (a challenge formula)

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who said:
A woman can appoint an agent
to receive her גט from the hand of her husband's agent.
But according to the one who said:
A woman cannot appoint an agent
to receive her גט from the hand of her husband's agent,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר: אִשָּׁה עוֹשָׂה שָׁלִיחַ לְקַבֵּל גִּיטָּהּ מִיָּד שְׁלִיחַ בַּעְלָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the revised case of step 13 according to one opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The step 13 setup, where she, as the husband's agent, gives the גט to her own receiving agent.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to the view that a wife's receiving agent may not take the גט from the husband's agent, this setup should not work.

steps.title: The rule is about the husband's honor, and here he doesn't mind
steps.stepSummary: The reason for forbidding a receiving agent here is that it shames the husband. In this case the husband himself arranged it, so he is not bothered.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Because it is a disgrace to the husband. And here the husband does not mind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by looking at the reason behind the strict opinion and showing that this reason does not apply in our case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband sent his own agent to hand the גט to the woman directly. Having her send a stand-in instead is insulting to him. Here the husband told her to appoint a receiving agent, so there is no insult, and even the strict opinion would agree.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Disgrace to the husband
He does not mind, is not particular

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Because there is a disgrace to the husband,
and here the husband does not mind.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא מַאי – מִשּׁוּם דְּאִיכָּא בִּזָּיוֹן דְּבַעַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14 by explaining the reason for the strict opinion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The reason for the rule does not apply in this case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The strict opinion would block any receiving agent from taking the גט from the husband's agent.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule exists only to protect the husband's honor. When the husband himself arranges it, the rule does not apply.

steps.title: What about the view that bases the rule on the חצר worry?
steps.stepSummary: The answer about the husband's honor works for one explanation of the strict rule. The גמרא asks what the other explanation, a worry about 'her courtyard acquired afterward', would say.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well according to the one who says the reason is the husband's disgrace. But according to the one who says it is because of 'her courtyard that comes afterward', what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 15 by pointing out that there is a second explanation for the strict rule, one that has nothing to do with the husband's feelings. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the rule is a protective decree, so that people won't mistakenly think a later-acquired חצר can receive a גט for her, then it does not matter whether the husband minds. So the answer from step 15 does not help according to this view.

keyTerms.meaning: Her courtyard, property that can acquire things for its owner
That comes afterward, acquired later

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who said:
it is because of the husband's disgrace;
but according to the one who said:
it is because of her courtyard that comes afterward,
phrases.notes: The worry is that people might think she could buy a courtyard where the husband already placed the גט and be divorced that way. That does not work.

phrases.english: what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר: מִשּׁוּם בִּזָּיוֹן דְּבַעַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 15's answer according to the other explanation of the strict rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 15's claim that the strict rule does not apply because the husband does not mind.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the rule is a decree because of the later-acquired חצר case, it does not depend on the husband's feelings, so his not minding changes nothing.

steps.title: She appoints a new delivery agent and receives the גט from him
steps.stepSummary: To satisfy the opinion that worries about 'her courtyard acquired afterward', the case is rebuilt so that she never has a receiving agent at all. She appoints another delivery agent for the husband, and she receives the גט from him herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is where the husband said to her: Be my agent to deliver this גט until you get there. When you get there, appoint another agent to deliver it, and then you receive your גט from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 16 by changing the case again. She hands the job to a new delivery agent for the husband, and she takes the גט from him as the wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 13 she appointed a שליח לקבלה, a receiving agent of her own. The opinion that worries about 'her courtyard acquired afterward' has a problem with that, and the husband's honor does not solve it. Now the new person is a שליח להולכה working for the husband, and she receives the גט directly with her own hands, so that worry never comes up.

keyTerms.meaning: appoint (make someone into)
an agent who delivers the גט on the husband's behalf
you arrive
receive (said to a woman)

phrases.english: Where he said to her: Be an agent for delivery
until you arrive there,
and when you arrive there,
appoint an agent for delivery,
and you receive your bill of divorce from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר לַהּ: הֱוַי שָׁלִיחַ לְהוֹלָכָה עַד דְּמָטְיַת הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 16 by changing the case again.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case so that the problem cannot come up
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed the case needed her to appoint a receiving agent, which this opinion forbids.
steps.terutzMaskana: She appoints a second delivery agent for the husband and receives the גט herself, so there is no receiving agent at all.

steps.title: She declares before the בית דין, and the court sends the גט to her
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: when she arrives, she makes the declaration 'בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם' before the בית דין. The court then appoints an agent who gives the גט to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: The husband told her: Be my delivery agent until you get there. When you get there, say before the court 'It was written in front of me and signed in front of me'. Then the court appoints an agent, and they give the גט to you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another way to set up the case. Here the בית דין, not the wife, picks the next delivery agent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As the husband's agent, she makes the required declaration that the גט was written and signed in her presence. The court then appoints a new delivery agent, who hands the גט to her as the wife. Her job as agent ends cleanly before she becomes the receiver, and she never appoints a receiving agent of her own.

keyTerms.meaning: 'and if you wish, say': introduces another possible answer
'it was written in my presence and signed in my presence': the declaration required of someone bringing a גט from abroad
the court (בית דין)
to you

steps.whatToRemember: Both answers keep the wife's role as the husband's agent separate from her role as the one receiving the גט. In both, she never appoints a receiving agent of her own.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say
that he said to her: Be an agent for delivery
until you arrive there,
and when you arrive there,
say before the court:
'It was written in my presence and signed in my presence,'
and the court appoints an agent,
and they will give it to you.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא, דְּאָמַר לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the קשיא of step 16, offered alongside step 17.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: She would need to appoint someone herself, either a receiving agent or a new delivery agent.
steps.terutzMaskana: The בית דין appoints the delivery agent after her declaration, and she receives the גט from that agent.

steps.title: הדרן: closing the chapter הַמֵּבִיא גֵּט
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the second chapter of גיטין, הַמֵּבִיא גֵּט.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter 'הַמֵּבִיא גֵּט'.
steps.whatsHappening: The chapter is over. This line marks its end and says goodbye to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no argument here. The הדרן ends the chapter about bringing a גט from abroad, and the next line begins a new topic.

keyTerms.meaning: 'we will return to you': the formula said at the end of a chapter
'One who brings a גט': the name of the second chapter

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'One who brings a bill of divorce'

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַרַן עֲלָךְ הַמֵּבִיא גֵּט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter whose discussion just ended.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter הַמֵּבִיא גֵּט is complete.

steps.title: A גט must be written for a specific woman: the marketplace example
steps.stepSummary: The new chapter's משנה rules that any גט not written for the sake of a specific woman is invalid. Its example is a man who hears scribes practicing a גט text that matches his own name and his wife's name.
steps.simpleTranslation: Any גט that was not written for a particular woman is invalid. How so? A man was walking through the market and heard scribes reading out a practice text: 'So-and-so divorces So-and-so from such-and-such place.' He said: That is my name, and that is my wife's name. That גט cannot be used to divorce her.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter begins with a משנה. It sets out the rule of לשמה: a גט must be written for the specific woman being divorced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scribes wrote the text as practice, not for any real couple. The names match exactly, but that does not help, because when it was written it was not meant for this woman. The rule depends on why the גט was written, not on whether the words are right.

keyTerms.meaning: for the sake of a specific woman (the idea of לִשְׁמָהּ)
invalid
scribes dictating or reading out a text, for example to students
so-and-so (a man / a woman)
how so? (introduces an example)

steps.confusionAlert: The names being exactly right does not make the גט valid. What matters is that it was written for this specific woman.
steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה is the source for the requirement of לשמה in writing a גט. The whole chapter is built on it.

phrases.english: Any bill of divorce that was written
not for the sake of a woman is invalid.
How so?
He was passing through the marketplace
and heard the voice of scribes dictating:
phrases.notes: The scribes are reading out a sample גט text, like a practice lesson, not writing for any real couple.

phrases.english: 'Man so-and-so divorces so-and-so
from place such-and-such,'

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר: זֶה שְׁמִי וְזֶה שֵׁם אִשְׁתִּי;
phrases.english: and he said: This is my name and that is my wife's name;
it is invalid for divorcing with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל גֵּט שֶׁנִּכְתַּב שֶׁלֹּא לְשׁוּם אִשָּׁה, פָּסוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new chapter after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט not written for the sake of a specific woman is invalid, even if the names happen to match.

steps.title: A real גט written for one couple cannot be used by another couple with the same names
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds a stronger case. A man wrote a גט to divorce his wife and then changed his mind. A neighbor has the same name, and the neighbor's wife has the same name as this man's wife. The neighbor still may not divorce his own wife with that גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even more than this: if a man wrote a גט to divorce his wife and then changed his mind, and a man from his town met him and said, 'My name is the same as yours, and my wife's name is the same as your wife's name,' that גט is invalid for divorcing with.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the rule of לשמה with a second, stronger example. A real גט, written for a real divorce, still cannot be moved over to a different couple, even when the names are identical.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 20 the גט was only practice writing, never meant for any real divorce. Here the גט was written seriously, but for a different woman, and the result is the same: it is פסול. Matching names do not help. What counts is which woman the גט was written for.

keyTerms.meaning: Even more than this. It introduces a stronger case of the same rule.
He changed his mind, or reconsidered.
A man from his town; a fellow townsman.
Invalid; it does not work.

steps.whatToRemember: A גט belongs to the woman it was written for. Even a fully serious גט with identical names cannot be used for a different woman, because it was not written לשמה, for her.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the problem is that the first man changed his mind. The גט is פסול for the neighbor because it was written for the first man's wife and not for the neighbor's wife.
steps.whyThisMatters: This case shows that לשמה is about who the writing was intended for, not about what the paper says. The rest of the chapter builds on this idea.

phrases.english: Even more than this:
if he wrote a גט to divorce his wife and then changed his mind,
and a man from his town found him and said to him:
My name is the same as your name
and my wife's name is the same as your wife's name;
it is invalid to divorce with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵר מִיכֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from step 20 with a stronger example of the same rule. It moves from a practice גט to a real גט written for a different woman.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט written for one man's wife, even seriously and for a real divorce, is פסול for another man to use for his own wife, even when both husbands' names and both wives' names are identical.
